68F414A8:
The annual Frith Amateur Shrub Pruning Contest proceeded as scheduled, but this time an astonishing event occurred. For a rookie reporter like the author, this scoop dropped from the heavens was an absolute godsend, and I rushed to the scene bounding like a follower beast leaping at bait.
Palum, visiting from the Rosia Empire, joined the contest at a friend's invitation and won first place with his entry, "The Perfect Square." However, right at that moment of celebration, immediately after receiving the award, he grabbed his pruning shears and charged toward the second-place entry. With just three cuts, the second-place entry, "Dancing Chimomo," was reduced to a "Sleek Little Ball," all its branches sheared off until the shrub became a perfectly round sphere.
Consequently, Palum was disqualified and stripped of his championship title for intentional destruction of another's work.
When asked about his motivation after the event, he replied that he was actually a bit of a perfectionist...
"My friend invited me to enter, saying 'Trim that into a square and you can earn some Unas.' It wasn't too hard so I finished quickly, but what the person next to me cut... I just couldn't stand it. Don't you feel annoyed looking at redundant branches? Ah, my cold sweat wouldn't stop, it was so unpleasant..."
"Shut up!"
Mid-interview, the creator of "Dancing Chimomo" rushed over and shouted,
"That's not a little ball, it's a Chimomo! Those branches aren't redundant! They're an abstract representation of Chimomo's tentacles!"
Amidst the fierce argument, other surrounding contestants and spectators turned to look one after another. Oh, looks like another fistfight is about to start. At least I won't run out of material for the next issue.
Anyway, the championship effectively went to third place—Paul, a young resident of Frith. His entry, titled "Blazing Art," was highly original: instead of pruning shears, he used flames to shape the shrub. The scorch marks scattered across the lush greenery were the scars of plants torn apart by fire, and the remaining branches and leaves extending upward alongside the scars demonstrated an indomitable life force, delivering a powerful impact to viewers. This work truly gave the most tangible expression to the pains of growth.
